content: AGENTS.md sits exactly at its frozen check:prose ceiling (92 violations), so any new bullet must add zero violations. The sentence counter splits per wrapped line and also splits on colon+space before a quote, so inline YAML/TS shape snippets like { method: 'x' } count as extra sentences and can push a bullet over long-paragraph(>6s). Describe the shape in prose instead and keep the literal in docs/design/warren-config.md. Each em-dash costs one dash violation. Verify with: bun run scripts/check-prose.ts --report | grep AGENTS

description: Adding one field to the mirrored CreateRunInput/DispatchRunInput pair in src/client/types.ts pushed the interface mirror over the scoped check:dups 40-token threshold
resolution: Re-declare the ergonomic interface as extends Omit of CreateRunInput plus the renamed keys (branch/provider/model) instead of adding to the allowlist: the field set is declared once, the clone disappears, and the list keeps shrinking.

description: Measuring `bun run check:coverage` in a sandbox where node_modules is MISSING produces an INFLATED coverage percentage, not a depressed one. When a test file fails to import ('Cannot find package drizzle-orm/zod/@os-eco/burrow-cli/...'), Bun's coverage reporter never imports the source under test, so that source is EXCLUDED from the denominator. A smaller denominator raises the %. A deps-missing sandbox reported lines 93.23% with ~208 import failures; the same repo deps-installed with ALL tests green (0 failures — exactly CI's state, since CI runs 'bun install' then 'check:coverage:ci') measured lines 92.21%. The patrol (warren-acd7) treated 93.23% as a lower bound and inferred CI >= 93.23%; the direction is inverted — 93.23% is an upper bound and CI is 92.21%. Setting a floor at (inflated_actual - margin) therefore breaks CI: a 92.98 lines floor failed because true CI coverage is 92.21%.
resolution: Before trusting any `bun run check:coverage` number for a ratchetwatch tightening: (1) run `bun install` first; (2) confirm the test run has ZERO failures (grep the summary for '0 fail' / no 'Cannot find package' errors) — import failures silently truncate the coverage denominator; (3) prefer reading the 'All files' row from a real CI run's coverage artifact over a sandbox measurement. Also: the _comment baseline note in scripts/coverage-budgets.json has been stale since 2026-06-12 (claims functions 88.85% while the floor is already 89.36) — keep it in sync when raising floors. Correct ratchet direction with true deps-installed actuals (functions 90.19% slack 0.83pt = FINDING; lines 92.21% slack 0.67pt = NOT a finding) is the OPPOSITE of what the inflated numbers suggested.

description: check-layers extension-boundary test (PR #799) asserted scan() findings in fixed array order; passed in the agent sandbox but failed on Linux CI because filesystem readdir order differs by platform. Walk-order is not deterministic across OSes — any multi-finding assertion over a directory walk must sort before comparing.
resolution: Repair run run_06ka61ctqz0j sorted findings (file,line) before asserting; commit 'test(check-layers): sort extension-boundary findings for walk-order determinism' on PR #799.

description: check-prose counts inline code spans stripped to 'CODE' as sentence starts, so backtick-heavy paragraphs get false long-paragraph violations
resolution: convert backtick-heavy explanatory paragraphs into bulleted lists, which are exempt from the >6-sentence paragraph rule

description: Fresh agent workspaces repeatedly failed root check:coverage because standalone extensions/judge dependencies were not installed; @sinclair/typebox was missing even though the changed campaign-controller package was green. Repeated full-gate reruns wasted substantial time.
resolution: Run bun run ext:install before check:all in a fresh workspace. Productize a bootstrap/preflight so the gate is self-sufficient or fails immediately; tracked in warren-0f90.

description: check-prose long-paragraph(>6s) counts sentence FRAGMENTS per wrapped source line, not real sentences: a 3-sentence paragraph wrapped across 6 lines with mid-line sentence ends read as 7. Also: moving a complexity-grandfathered function to a new file re-exposes noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity (grandfather list is per-file).
resolution: Align sentence boundaries to line ends, avoid '..' in prose, and refactor moved functions below complexity 15 rather than adding to biome.json overrides.

content: When a warren union merge pushes files past the 500-line check:size budget, fix by splitting cohesive slices into sibling dotted-grouping modules and re-exporting so import paths stay stable (see analytics.projection.ts, run-metrics.economics.test.ts from warren-ea4e). For check:bundle-size, raw bytes are toolchain-stable but the pod's bun (1.2.23) gzips cooler than CI's (.bun-version 1.3.14); install bun 1.3.14 (~/.local/bin), rm -rf src/ui/node_modules, rebuild frozen, then check:bundle-size --update auto-raises within cap. Budget edits are never hand-written. Also: jscpd allowlist pairs must track where duplicated code moves (scripts/dups-allowlist.json), and stale __golden__ analytics fixtures must be regenerated with WARREN_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1.

description: On macOS hosts, check:coverage fails via the environment-sensitive readyz runtime test (expects no-bwrap => 503, gets 200 under full-suite order; passes standalone). Pre-existing, Linux CI green. Tracked as warren-4de5.
resolution: Not yet fixed — tracked as warren-4de5. For release commits on macOS, use git commit --no-verify and document the bypass in the commit message; CI remains the authoritative gate.

description: A test that runs git commit without a repo-local or -c identity passes on macOS and fails on the Linux CI runner with 'empty ident name'. macOS git auto-detects a name from the account's full name; the runner user has none. An empty HOME does NOT reproduce it locally.
resolution: Pass -c user.name/-c user.email in the test's git helper, or use createGitFixture (sets a repo-local identity). Reproduce CI locally with a fake HOME whose .gitconfig sets user.useConfigOnly=true (GIT_* env vars are scrubbed by the fixture helpers, so use the file).
